main_text.p: pontifices & alii ex praesulibus Romanis, tamen eos exercere multos alios actus pastorales; ligando, solvendo, controversias diiudicando: praeterea facere per alios, quod per se concionando facere nequeunt. Resp. Hujusmodi potestatem vel potius licentiam non permittunt literae. Audi etiam Maldonatum Jesuitam in summul. qu. 10. artic. 3. 5. 6. Notarunt, inquit, Hieronymus & Augustinus, propterea Paulum nō distinxisse pastores & doctores, quia omnis potestas debet docere, & nomen pastoris significat actionem personalem, sicut nomen medici. Itaq; sicut nemo potest per alium curare, ita nemo potest suas oves per alium pascere. nec quic-quam valet responsio communis, satis esse per vicarium laborare, quia secundum eandem regulam satis esset manducare per vicariū: quia scriptum est. Qui non laborat, non manducet. Quibus assentitur Episcopus Espensaeus com. in Tit. 1. & 1. ad Tim. digress. l. 2. c. 23. Adjecit, inquit, apo-

page.notes: Printed page 212 (top centre). The right-hand strip showing "apostol...", "Hieron..." etc. belongs to the neighbouring printed page and was left out. Italic passages: the opening line group, "Maldonatum Jesuitam ...", "inquit" (twice), and the citation "Episcopus Espensaeus com. in Tit. 1. & 1. ad Tim. digress. l. 2. c. 23." The words "apo-" at the foot are a catchword split by a hyphen. A small faint mark near the bottom centre is a stain, not text. Doubtful: "Hu;usmodi" is printed with a j-like form, read as "Hujusmodi"; "Espensaeus" and the paragraph break (no indent visible, so treated as one paragraph) are my readings. The fold/shadow on the left edge is not printed text.
